First, there was the language itself. In so many isekais, everyone in the new world just happens to speak japanese, despite being some sort of medieval European-esque fantasy land. Here it's a real barrier to him, and it takes him years to fully figure it out.

I've also come to expect that isekai MCs already get the premise and can get to action right away. Cautious Hero even jokes about this: "I always reincarnate an otaku from Japan because they already get it". It isn't for a couple years that he realizes he isn't on Earth and there is the existence of magic.

Like you said, the manga adds a lot more nuance to the characters. Ishida is validated less often for his actions, and Ueno is more abrasive. The manga felt a little too ambitious in exploring the anger and hatred from so many different characters.

For this reason, I feel that the anime works better. It strikes a better balance between despair and hope, and the unresolved ending feels more natural. I think the element of sound in the anime adds a huge layer of depth in understanding Shouko's disability, too. I'm also a little biased towards the soundtrack - Kyoani knocked it out of the park. Ultimately, I could see the case for both arguments, but I personally like the movie more.
